findings.title: Rule 6 still accepts a landing record the closer hand-writes, and br close --transition-comment makes that a one-liner that skips close-gate
findings.evidence: Boundary: comment text written by the agent -> check 35 rule 6. Rule 6 now asks only that some comment NEW in this commit start with 'GATE:', 'FRESH-VERIFY:' or 'TRIAGE-CLOSE:' (lines 249-252). The .15 change adopts br 0.5.12's `--transition-comment` flag (confirmed by `br close --help`), so an agent can run `br close <id> --reason 'shipped' --transition-comment 'GATE: receipt'` and never call close-gate at all: no RED receipt, no probes, no scanner, no ownership check. Rule 6 sees one new GATE:-prefixed comment and passes. The same works with `br comments add <id> 'GATE: x'` followed by a plain `br close`. The round-2 finding was 'any historical or hand-written record'. The .16 by-identity key fixes the historical half only, and the rule 6 tests (35-board-integrity.test.sh) never feed it a hand-written record.
findings.fix: Make rule 6 check the record's grammar, not just its prefix. Require the full close-gate shape, `^(GATE: (receipt|decided)|FRESH-VERIFY:|TRIAGE-CLOSE:) — <id> — .* (verified )?at <sha> by <actor> at <ISO ts>`, where <id> is the row's own id, <sha> resolves and is an ancestor of the staged commit, and <actor> is the row's assignee (for GATE: decided, a name on the Humans line or ac-tidy). A stronger option: close-gate appends a line to <git-common-dir>/ac-close-ledger (id, record sha256, HEAD) and rule 6 requires the record's hash to be in that ledger. Add a rule-6 test in which a bare 'GATE: receipt' comment is new in the commit and must FAIL.

findings.title: ac-tidy exemption never checks the ruling says 'moot', and it keys on labels any agent can add at close time
findings.evidence: Boundary: bead labels and comment text, both agent-mutable -> the ruling path. Lines 205-206 set AUTHORIZED=1 when the actor is 'ac-tidy' and the live board carries 'pipeline-proposal'. The canon (bead-conventions.md:226-232) allows only `DECISION (ac-tidy): moot`, but the ruling text is never checked. Routing (line 191) and the exemption (line 206) both read the LIVE labels. So any agent can close any task or bug bead with no probe legs: `br label add <id> human-gate pipeline-proposal; br comments add <id> 'DECISION (ac-tidy): shipped'; close-gate.sh <id> --reason 'decided: x'`. The gate then writes a genuine-looking `GATE: decided ... ruling verified` record, which also satisfies rule 6. Plan risk R1 covers forged HUMAN names only. This path needs no human impersonation, uses the one agent identity the gate explicitly trusts, and gets around the 'moot only' limit. The tests (close-gate.test.sh:371-386) cover only the literal 'moot' text and the missing-label case, never non-moot ac-tidy text.
findings.fix: Require the ac-tidy ruling to match exactly: `[ "$RULING" = 'DECISION (ac-tidy): moot' ]` (allowing only an optional ' — <why>' suffix). Take the routing type/labels and the pipeline-proposal label from the COMMITTED board (`git show HEAD:.beads/issues.jsonl`) rather than the live row, so a label added during the session cannot move a bead onto the no-probe path. Add a test where `DECISION (ac-tidy): approved` must be refused.

findings.title: Any genuine human DECISION ever posted becomes close authority after a live relabel or reopen (retype bypass without forgery)
findings.evidence: Boundary: live issue_type/labels plus the whole comment history -> the ruling path. Routing reads the live type/labels (lines 185-191), and RULING takes the first authorized DECISION line from ANY comment in the bead's history (line 200). It ignores when the comment was posted relative to a reopen or a relabel, and it ignores what the ruling says. Concrete path with no R1 forgery: Craig writes `DECISION (Craig): use approach A — ...` as guidance on a task bead (action-loop.md:18 is the documented idiom), or rules on a human-gate bead that is later reopened. The agent then runs `br update <id> --type decision` (or adds `human-gate`) and calls close-gate. The real ruling is 'verified', no probe leg runs, and the gate writes `GATE: decided`. That is the round-2 retype bypass, still alive for every bead that carries a real human ruling. Rule 6 was fixed (.16) to reject a stale record from before a reopen; the ruling matcher did not get the same fix.
findings.fix: Take the routing type/labels from the committed HEAD board, not the live row, so a retype or relabel in the same session cannot route. Accept only a ruling comment created after the bead's most recent status transition to open/in_progress (compare its created_at against the latest reopen event, or against HEAD's board snapshot, the same by-identity 'new since HEAD' logic rule 6 uses). Add tests: (a) a task bead relabelled human-gate mid-session carrying an old Craig ruling must be refused; (b) a reopened decision bead with only its pre-reopen ruling must be refused.

findings.title: Scanner baseline tree comes from an unauthenticated receipt file, is read even when LEG 1 rejected that receipt, and is never checked to predate the bead's work; inert today only because real ubs prints absolute paths
findings.evidence: Boundary: <git-common-dir>/ac-flight/<id>.flight-receipt, a plain append-only file the worker can write -> the scanner rescue. Line 576 reads `tree:` from the LAST receipt block. That happens even when LEG 1 set FRESH_VERIFY=1 because the receipt was unusable (missing red-probe, or bead mismatch, line 345). The only validation is `git cat-file -e ${BASE_TREE}^{commit}`: no check that the tree is a strict ancestor of HEAD, and no check that it differs from HEAD. worker.md puts section 6 COMMIT before section 7 CLOSE, so at close time HEAD already contains the bead's code. Appending `FLIGHT-RECEIPT v1\ntree: $(git rev-parse HEAD)` sets the baseline to the bead's own diff, and every new finding counts as 'pre-existing'. A second problem: line 629 matches with a set test (`grep -qxF`), not a multiset, so N new copies of a line that already exists in the file all match one base signature. Measured with real ubs 5.4.2: DETAIL lines carry ABSOLUTE paths (`/tmp/ubsprobe.ARgN/b.py :: py.eval-exec: ...` at HEAD against `/tmp/ubsprobe.ARgN/base/b.py :: ...` from the scratch-dir base scan). HEAD and base signatures therefore never match, so the rescue never fires against real ubs today (it fails closed). AC4b passes only because the mock ubs echoes relative paths. When someone fixes the path prefix, the steerable-baseline hole opens immediately.
findings.fix: (1) Use BASE_TREE only when FRESH_VERIFY=0, meaning the receipt is the one LEG 1 accepted. (2) Require `git merge-base --is-ancestor $BASE_TREE HEAD` and `$BASE_TREE != $(git rev-parse HEAD)`. Better still, require it to equal the tree on the receipt comment posted to the bead at claim time, which is board state rather than a local file. (3) Remove the $ROOT/ and $SCRATCH/ prefixes from the path before building the signature. (4) Match as a multiset: count occurrences of each signature at HEAD and at base, and count max(0, head-base) as new. (5) Add a test with a real ubs-shaped absolute-path fixture, and a test where a receipt `tree:` equal to HEAD must NOT rescue anything.
